playbook: Sales playbook: Example Booking Software, annual multi-location plans

header.business: Example Booking Software, an online booking and scheduling app for small service businesses (invented example)

mature_cohort.rule: max(30, 90th percentile of created-to-won days among won deals)

header.team: 2 account executives starting 2026-11-02, quota $60,000 new annual contract value each per quarter, 12 selling weeks a quarter

1_who_to_target.method: Value per opportunity = win rate x average won amount, from the mature cohort. Target when at or above the overall $1,742; disqualify under half of it; work in between; unproven under 10 mature opportunities.

top_loss_reasons.reason: Too small for an annual plan

target_profile.evidence: tiers above, from the mature cohort

disqualify.rule: send to the monthly self-serve plan; do not open an opportunity
disqualify.evidence: 0 won of 13 mature opportunities, value per opportunity $0; top loss reason: Too small for an annual plan (4)

if_disqualified_segments_are_dropped.note: Shown, not used: the activity math below keeps the all-segment rates until a quarter of data confirms these.

2_stages.method: Conversion = deals that reached the next stage / deals that reached this one and left it. Stall limit = 90th percentile of days in the stage among deals that moved on, at least 3.

stages.exit_criteria: the owner or operations lead has been on a call, and the demo is booked on that call
stages.evidence: call standards: owner on the first call and next meeting booked on the call (coded notes)

stages.exit_criteria: the decision maker saw the demo and named who else signs; amount and expected close date are set
the proposal is sent and the buyer has replied with questions or changes
terms agreed and the order form is out for signature

2_stages.rule: Past the stall limit, the owner sets a dated next step or closes the deal lost with a reason.

rates_used.rate: Inbound and referral opportunities a week

math_per_rep_per_quarter: Inbound opportunities = 3.0 a week x 12 weeks / 2 reps = 18.0
Outbound opportunities = 3.35 / 0.148 = 22.6 a quarter, or 1.89 a week

weekly_per_rep.note: Rounded up for display; the chain uses unrounded figures. Touches count the steps of the proposed cadence (section 4). The reply rate is kept as measured; the cut step drew 2.7% of replies.

capacity_check.verdict: Research fits (27 new prospects a day against 30). Calls do not fit: the cadence's 2 phone steps need 54 calls a day against the 40 you estimated. Run the phone steps only for target-tier accounts, or add SDR time; recheck after 4 weeks of real call counts.
capacity_check.source: capacity figures are the founder's estimate: assumption to test

lead_time.meaning: Prospects contacted today become opportunities about 18 days later and wins about 41 days after that, so a quarter's outbound has to start about 59 days before the quarter's last day.

4_cadence.rule: A step with 200 or more sends that draws under 5% of all replies is cut or rewritten.
4_cadence.copy: Message copy comes from the cold email and LinkedIn message skills (see linked guides).

5_call_and_email_standards.method: Win rate with and without each behaviour across coded notes of closed deals. A standard needs 8 or more deals on each side and a gap of 10 points or more; otherwise it stays an assumption to test.

behaviours.behaviour: The owner or operations lead was on the first call
The pain was put in numbers (no-shows a week, front-desk hours)
The next meeting was booked before the call ended
A written recap went out within 1 business day

standards: The owner or operations lead was on the first call

to_test: The pain was put in numbers (no-shows a week, front-desk hours)

rules.rule: Every open deal has an expected close date in the future; moving it needs a one-line reason.
rules.found_today: 8 of 29 open deals have a close date in the past

rules.rule: Every open deal has a dated next step.
An amount is set before a deal leaves Discovery.

Loss reason is a required picklist with no Other option: Chose Competitor A, Chose Competitor B, Chose the monthly self-serve plan, No decision, Price, Staying with current tool, Timing, Too small for an annual plan
rules.found_today: 12 of 65 lost deals (18.5%) are blank or Other

rules.rule: A deal past its stage's stall limit gets a dated next step or is closed lost.
rules.found_today: 9 open deals are past their stage's limit

rules.rule: Outbound deals keep the first-touch date, so lead time can be measured.

6_crm_hygiene.weekly: Each rep clears these before the Monday pipeline review.

phases.focus: learn the product and the target profile; sit in on founder calls; pass a role play on the call guide and the top 3 objections; from day 15, outbound at half the weekly prospect target
full weekly activity; runs own discovery and demos; inbound routed in from day 31; CRM rules every Monday
full cycle alone: proposals and negotiation; founder joins only target-tier deals over the average won amount ($6,792), a proposal to test

7_ramp_30_60_90.milestone_method: Outcomes lag contacts by the cadence length (24 days): meetings and outbound opportunities by a date come from prospects contacted 24 days earlier, at the team's rates. Inbound opportunities from day 31 at the per-rep weekly rate. Estimates.

first_expected_win.label: estimate
first_expected_win.math: day 31 (2026-12-02) + median 41 days created to won

7_ramp_30_60_90.quota_ramp_rule: Quarters ending before the first expected win carry no quota; the quarter it falls in carries quota x the share of its days from that date to its end; full quota after. Estimates: share to 3 decimals, quota to the whole dollar.

8_linked_guides.part: Cold call opener, discovery guide and demo flow
Inbound lead handoff and response time
Why deals are won and lost, in depth
